region: Ladakh: Leh, Hemis National Park, the Sham valley
title: India (Ladakh) — Snow Leopards, Oracles and Frozen Villages
subtitle: Fifteen days in the Himalayan winter: two oracle festivals, tracking in Hemis and Ulley from family homestays at minus 20
summary: A winter expedition around Leh: the Stok and Matho oracle festivals, snow leopard tracking from village homestays in Rumbak and Ulley, and a quiet western loop through Likir, Alchi and Lamayuru. Intentionally avoids the border zones, the roads closed in winter and the standard Leh monastery circuit.
introduction: In February the roads into Ladakh are shut and the only way in is a morning flight to Leh at 3,500 m. The route spends three days acclimatising, then joins Stok's Guru Tsechu on 15-16 February, when the village's oracle goes into a trance. It walks into Rumbak, a snowbound village in Hemis National Park, where families host snow leopard watchers and local spotters scan the slopes for bharal and the cat. After the Matho oracle festival, a loop west through Ulley, Likir, Alchi and Lamayuru ends with ice in the gorges. Nights fall to minus 20.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was a self-drive journey in a warm desert with tents; here nobody drives, the road network is mostly closed and the nights are 40 degrees colder. The expedition is on foot and by local taxi, sleeping in family homes rather than tents, and the main risk is cold and altitude rather than distance.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Ladakh is sold as a summer circuit of Pangong, Nubra and the big monasteries. In February those routes are closed or empty and the offer is a few expensive snow leopard packages (about USD 2,663 for 10 days without flights). This plan reaches the same villages through community homestays, with two festivals and a loop in the west that few visitors see in winter.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio combines a Himalayan winter, trance oracle festivals timed to a lunar calendar and a realistic chance to see a snow leopard from a family house at 3,900 m.

duration.note: Day 1 night flight Paris-Delhi, day 15 arrival in Paris after the night flight from Delhi. Leh flights are weather-dependent, so days 13 and 14 are a buffer.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: The window brackets the Stok Guru Tsechu (15-16 Feb) and Matho Nagrang (about 19-20 Feb) and sits in the core snow leopard season. The same dates give 48 hours of acclimatisation before Stok. March is milder, but the festivals are over.

februarySuitability.summary: Coldest month: Leh averages about -9 C at night and villages above 3,800 m reach -20 C or lower. Festivals and snow leopard season peak, but flights and roads are weather-dependent and the Chadar river walk is unreliable.

marchSuitability.summary: Milder (Leh daytime near 10 C) and snow leopards are still tracked, but the Stok and Matho festivals are over and melt makes village tracks muddy. Better for the Sham loop than for the main concept.

climate.regionNote: Leh normals 1951-2020 at 3,513 m (Wikipedia climate table); villages such as Rumbak (about 3,900 m) and Ulley (about 3,900 m) are colder, with night lows of -15 to -25 C reported by operators.

february.rainfall: About 8 mm precipitation in Leh, almost all snow; dry, sunny air.
february.notes: Leh mean max 4.2 C, mean min -9.2 C. In villages water pipes freeze; heating is a yak-dung or wood stove in the kitchen only.

march.rainfall: About 11 mm in Leh, snow and sleet.
march.notes: Leh mean max 9.7 C, mean min -3.7 C. Snow begins to melt on south-facing slopes.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: The Srinagar-Leh road over Zoji La and the Manali-Leh road are closed in winter and Leh is reached only by air. Khardung La, Chang La and the Pangong road are reported open at times and closed after snowfall; not used here. The Chadar (frozen Zanskar) was suspended in 2026 for lack of ice.
climate.airQuality: Excellent in Ladakh. Delhi has poor winter air quality and fog that delays flights; a buffer day is built in.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Snow leopards come down with bharal and ibex in winter; sightings are mostly reported between November and March, and peak in January-February. Sightings are never guaranteed.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Dosmochey (Leh, Likir, Diskit)
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Before the arrival date; Leh festival is a flexible bonus only if flights move.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Stok Guru Tsechu
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: 15-16 Feb 2027 (reported by two operator sites, not confirmed by an official calendar)
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Anchors day 5-6; oracles (lhamo) perform on the second day. Confirm with the monastery 2-3 weeks before travel.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Matho Nagrang
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Anchors day 9-10; the two Matho oracles are the centre of the rite. The Gregorian date can shift by a day because it follows the Tibetan lunar calendar.

climate.ramadan2027: Mostly not relevant for the route: villages are Buddhist. About 15% of Leh district is Muslim, so some Muslim-run cafés in Leh may shorten daytime opening between about 8 Feb and 9 Mar 2027.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Tibetan New Year (Losar) derives to about 7 Feb 2027 from the Tsechu date; Ladakhi villages celebrate their own Losar earlier (reported 28 December), so no closures in the window.
climate.tourismDemand: Very low: the winter economy depends on a few snow leopard and festival visitors. Many Leh hotels are closed; heated guesthouses and homestays are open.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: February is described as a low-fare month for Delhi-Leh; Paris-Delhi fares in February 2027 start from about EUR 523 on connecting itineraries.

geography.summary: Cold-desert Himalaya at 3,500-4,000 m along the Indus: bare mountains, flat-roofed villages in irrigated side valleys and gorges that freeze in winter.
geography.distinctive: Hemis National Park, south of Leh, has one of the densest known snow leopard populations in the world and can be entered on foot from the road end at Zingchen to a village inside the park where families keep a homestay. The western loop crosses the eroded lake sediments of the Lamayuru Moonland.

landscapes.name: Rumbak gorge and Hemis National Park
landscapes.description: Frozen stream, bare rock slopes with bharal and ibex, willow thickets. Peaks above 6,000 m border the park.

landscapes.name: Indus valley between Leh and Alchi
landscapes.description: Snow-edged river, apricot orchards in fall colour or bare, villages on terraces.

landscapes.name: Lamayuru Moonland and Wanla gorge
landscapes.description: Eroded lake sediments around Lamayuru and a narrow canyon road to Wanla that ices over in February.

landscapes.name: Ulley valley
landscapes.description: Remote side valley north of the Indus with ibex, bharal and a resident snow leopard population.

culture.summary: Tibetan Buddhist Ladakh in its winter: monasteries that open on festival days, oracle rituals that survive only in a few villages and farming families who spend the cold months hosting.

culturalHighlights.name: Stok Guru Tsechu
culturalHighlights.description: Two-day monastic festival of masked cham dances to honour Guru Padmasambhava. On the second day two oracles, women who are trained mediums, enter a trance and answer questions. Photography and behaviour rules are set by the monastery: sit where the monks direct, do not touch the oracles.

culturalHighlights.name: Matho Nagrang
culturalHighlights.description: Held at Matho Monastery (Sakya order) on the 15th day of the first Tibetan month. The two village oracles enter a trance, are blindfolded and move along the roofs; the rite is said to foretell the year. It is a religious event, not a performance, and the oracles are not to be photographed intrusively.

culturalHighlights.name: Alchi Choskhor and Sumtsek
culturalHighlights.description: Monastery complex founded by Rinchen Zangpo, with wall paintings in the Sumtsek from the 11th-12th centuries in a Kashmiri-influenced style. In winter it is visited with a caretaker; the interior is unheated and photography is restricted.

culturalHighlights.name: Likir Monastery
culturalHighlights.description: Gelug monastery above the Sham valley with a large Maitreya statue; winter is the quietest period, and monks hold prayers daily.

culturalHighlights.name: Lamayuru and Wanla Gompas
culturalHighlights.description: Lamayuru is among the oldest Ladakhi monasteries on a ridge above the Moonland; Wanla's small gompa on a cliff overlooks a gorge village.

culturalHighlights.name: Winter homestays in Rumbak, Stok and Ulley
culturalHighlights.description: Family houses in which guests sit in the kitchen with the stove, eat dal and tsampa, and pay the household. The community homestay scheme was set up by the Snow Leopard Conservancy India Trust to share tourism income and reduce conflict over livestock.

adventureHighlights.name: Winter walk-in to Rumbak
adventureHighlights.description: About 7-8 km on a snow-covered track from the Zingchen road end to Rumbak at about 3,900 m (distance and ascent approximate; to be confirmed with the host). Mules carry bags. Crampons or microspikes may be needed on iced sections.

adventureHighlights.name: Snow leopard tracking from a homestay
adventureHighlights.description: Dawn and dusk sessions on foot and by scope with local spotters on slopes at 3,900-4,300 m, in -15 C or colder. Sessions are mostly sitting still, which is the hardest part in the cold.

adventureHighlights.name: Winter driving on icy roads
adventureHighlights.description: The Indus road and the Wanla canyon road are plowed but icy in places. A local driver with chains handles it; nobody on the team drives.

signatureExperiences.title: Snow leopard tracking from Rumbak and Ulley
signatureExperiences.description: Three nights in Rumbak homestays inside Hemis National Park with two full tracking days, then a dawn session at Ulley in the Sham valley. Local spotters locate bharal herds and scan with scopes from fixed viewpoints. Rumbak is the main base; Ulley is a second site in case the first is quiet.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Snow leopards are seen from a family home at 3,900 m on foot, not from a jeep. Fees go to the household and to spotters, which is the Conservancy's model.
signatureExperiences.location: Rumbak (Hemis National Park) and Ulley, Sham valley
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book through a Leh-based operator registered with the Ladakh tour operators' association or directly with Himalayan Homestays, who host in Sham, Rong and Zanskar; the operator arranges the Hemis winter permit from the Wildlife Office in Leh. Package examples start at USD 2,663 for 10 days without flights; DIY with local spotters costs far less. Allow 2-3 sighting days; success is not guaranteed.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Homestays 4 nights (80), spotters (60), park and permit (30), guide share (60), taxi share (50), gear rental (40), buffer (10). Estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Stok Guru Tsechu and Matho Nagrang oracle festivals
signatureExperiences.description: Two oracle festivals within five days. At Stok (15-16 Feb) masked cham dances and a trance rite; at Matho (about 19-20 Feb) the two village oracles run the Nagrang rite on the monastery roofs.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Matho's Nagrang is one of the few oracle festivals in the Himalaya; the winter dates mean very few foreign visitors and the monastery full of villagers.
signatureExperiences.location: Stok and Matho, 15-26 km from Leh
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local taxi from Leh with a guide who explains the rites; monasteries do not charge entry for festivals but donations are expected. The dates follow the Tibetan lunar calendar and two operator sites agree on them; verify with the monastery or the Ladakh tourism office two to three weeks before travel.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Taxi and donations; guide cost counted under guides. Estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Winter village life: homestays at minus 20
signatureExperiences.description: Five nights in family homes in Stok, Rumbak and Ulley. Evenings are in the kitchen with the stove, with butter tea and thukpa; bedrooms are unheated and guests need a -20 C sleeping bag; water is from a flask; the toilet is a dry latrine outside.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Winter is the season when families are at home and the only visitors are snow leopard watchers; the stay is the culture, not a performance.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book via Himalayan Homestays or a Leh operator; payment directly to the household in cash. Bring sleeping bag liners and a thermos; the host decides meal times.
signatureExperiences.costNote: 5 nights at about EUR 20 with dinner and breakfast. Estimate from press-quoted homestay rates.

signatureExperiences.title: Western Sham loop in winter: Likir, Alchi, Lamayuru and Wanla
signatureExperiences.description: One day by taxi along the Indus: Likir, then the Sumtsek wall paintings at Alchi, a night at Lamayuru and the frozen canyon to Wanla. Ibex are often seen on the cliffs near Khalsi.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The route most visitors do in July is empty in February; monks have time and the Moonland is under snow.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local taxi (union rules); winter opening of Alchi's temples depends on the caretaker, so the driver phones ahead.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Taxi share (two days) 25, Lamayuru night 35, entries 10, guide share 20. Estimate.

travelStyle.summary: Local taxi with driver, a walked access to Rumbak and homestays throughout; nobody drives or rides a motorbike.

transport.summary: Fly Delhi-Leh in the morning; inside Ladakh use a union taxi with a driver. Outside taxis cannot do local sightseeing under union practice and self-drive rentals are not available for the group's plan.

modes.description: Morning flights from Delhi operated by IndiGo and Air India, weather-dependent: snowfall has temporarily suspended Leh landings in January 2026.

modes.mode: Local union taxi (SUV or Innova with chains)
modes.description: Fares are route-based; booked through a Leh operator or guesthouse. Winter rates are not published online.
About 3-4 hours from the Zingchen road end; mules carry the bags.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental is not recommended: Ladakh taxi union practice bars outside commercial and rented vehicles from local sightseeing; winter road conditions are severe. Use a local taxi with driver.

drivingRequirements.summary: Not feasible or advisable: black ice, 4,000 m heights, taxi-union rules, and only two of the four hold a car licence.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: An International Driving Permit (1949 Convention) plus national licence would be required for any self-drive in India; not used in this plan.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four travellers hold a car licence; the plan needs none.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorbikes: Ladakh is known for motorbike tours but nobody holds a motorcycle licence and roads are icy in February. Legal alternatives: passenger in a taxi, guided walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Local taxi with driver, booked through a Leh operator, with winter chains and a driver who knows the Wanla road.

accommodation.summary: Heated guesthouses in Leh and Lamayuru, family homestays in Stok, Rumbak and Ulley, Delhi airport hotel for two nights. Bedrooms in villages are unheated.

camping.summary: Camping at -20 C in a national park in February is a safety risk; homestays are the intended accommodation.

physicalDifficulty.label: strenuous
physicalDifficulty.summary: Altitude from 3,500 m to about 4,300 m, nights to -20 C, a 3-4 hour walk-in in snow and long sitting at viewpoints. Moderate fitness plus acclimatisation; no technical skills. Acute mountain sickness is the main danger.

itinerary.summary: Fifteen days: two travel days to Delhi and Leh, two acclimatisation days in Leh, the Stok festival, three nights in Rumbak, the Matho festival, a night in Ulley, a night in Lamayuru and two buffer days for flights.

activities: Overnight flight CDG-DEL; buy a single ticket to protect the connection
days.transport: Flight CDG-DEL (Air France or Air India direct, or via a Gulf hub)
days.practical: Check the e-Visa (apply 4-30 days before) and the e-Arrival card (from 72 h before travel). Airlines and times not verified.

days.title: Delhi rest day before the Leh flight
activities: Buy a SIM at the airport if needed; do not carry a satellite device
days.practical: Leh flights leave in the morning, so a Delhi night is needed. Delhi winter fog can delay flights.

days.title: Fly to Leh at 3,500 m, rest
activities: Check in, drink water, no alcohol, no exertion
days.geographicalHighlight: Zanskar and Stok ranges from the plane
days.practical: Acclimatisation is mandatory: 48 h before going to higher areas. Tell a doctor in advance if you want acetazolamide.

days.title: Acclimatisation: old town and Leh Palace
activities: Slow walk in the old town
Optional ice hockey match if a local league game is played (2026 league ran 29 Jan-14 Feb; 2027 schedule unconfirmed)
days.practical: Stay below 3,600 m today. Check for headaches, nausea, sleep problems.

days.title: Stok Guru Tsechu, first day
activities: Walk the village with a local guide
days.practical: 48 h of acclimatisation completed this morning. Bring warm layers: the courtyard is open.

days.title: Stok oracle day, then the walk to Rumbak
activities: Oracle rite on the second day
Walk to Rumbak (3-4 h) with mules for the bags
days.practical: Hemis winter permit arranged in advance by the operator. If snow blocks the track, the group walks from a lower point.

days.title: Snow leopard tracking, day 1
activities: Dawn and dusk viewpoints with local spotters
days.travelTime: Up to 3 h round trip per session
days.practical: Sit still in -15 C or colder; bring chemical hand warmers and a spare layer. Retreat if frostbite signs appear.

days.title: Snow leopard tracking, day 2 (flexible)
activities: Second tracking day, move to a different viewpoint
Option to swap for a rest day if anyone shows altitude symptoms
days.travelTime: Up to 3 h round trip per session
days.practical: This is the contingency day for sightings and weather.

days.title: Out of Rumbak to Matho
activities: Drive to Matho (about 26 km from Leh), first day of Nagrang
days.practical: Matho has few rooms; a Leh guesthouse is the fallback.

days.title: Nagrang oracles, then to Ulley
activities: Taxi to the Sham valley via Leh
days.practical: Plan the transfer after the oracle rite; leave by early afternoon to arrive before dark.

days.title: Ulley dawn, then Likir, Alchi and Lamayuru
days.practical: Ask the driver to phone the Alchi caretaker; interiors may be locked in winter.

days.title: Wanla gorge and back to Leh
activities: Return to Leh and hot shower
days.practical: If the canyon road is blocked, skip Wanla and go straight to Leh.

activities: Morning flight IXL-DEL; the next day is a buffer if it is cancelled
days.practical: Snowfall can stop Leh flights for a day: IndiGo posted such a suspension on 5 January 2026.

days.title: Delhi day, night flight to Paris
activities: Old Delhi and Humayun's Tomb if energy allows
days.practical: Second buffer: if Leh flights slipped, this day absorbs it.

lines.label: Heated guesthouses/hotels in Leh, Lamayuru and Delhi, 2 twin rooms
lines.note: 7 nights x 2 rooms = 14 room-nights (Leh x4, Lamayuru x1, Delhi x2). Winter rates in Leh are low because most hotels are closed; the heated guesthouses that stay open quote roughly INR 2,500-5,000 per room (planning assumption, about INR 100 per EUR; no quote obtained).

lines.note: 5 homestay nights per person. Press guides quote about INR 800-1,050 per person with meals in Rumbak; Ulley lodge-style stays cost more. Comfortable = Ulley snow leopard lodge rates (estimate).

lines.note: 15 days x EUR 14. Dal-bhat, momos, thukpa, butter tea; Delhi street food. Planning assumption, not a quote.

lines.label: Boiled or filtered water, bottled water in Leh and Delhi

The Ladakh taxi union fixes route-based fares; no official rate card was obtained, so these are estimates (INR 3,600-7,500 per day). Winter fares are not published online.

lines.note: Down parkas and boots weigh 3-4 kg; assume one prepaid extra 10 kg on the domestic sector.

security.summary: France Diplomatie, the UK FCDO and Canada do not advise against travel to Ladakh and the US reportedly excepts Leh from its Jammu and Kashmir Level 4. The Netherlands, however, marks the India-China border area in Ladakh orange, and there was deadly unrest in Leh in September 2025 with the political dispute unresolved. The route avoids Pangong, Hanle and Nubra, but the conflict between sources, recent unrest and flight dependence keep it conditional.
security.assessedRoute: Leh, Stok, Rumbak (Hemis NP), Matho, Ulley, Likir, Alchi, Lamayuru, Wanla; flights Delhi-Leh. Excludes Srinagar-Leh and Manali-Leh roads, Nubra, Pangong Tso, Hanle, Tso Moriri, Turtuk and the Line of Actual Control.

advisories.level: Red (formellement déconseillé): Kashmir valley and the immediate surroundings of the LoC and the Pakistan border; Srinagar-Leh road. Ladakh itself: no colour, with advice to avoid the zones next to the China border and to follow the rules for military installations
advisories.regionsAffected: Valley of Kashmir; LoC; India-Pakistan border; Srinagar-Leh road
advisories.routeImpact: Route enters none of these; arrival is by air.

advisories.level: Against all travel to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and within 10 km of the India-Pakistan border; Ladakh is not listed
advisories.routeImpact: Ladakh is a separate Union Territory and is not covered; still current 28 Nov 2026.

advisories.level: Yellow for India overall; orange for the India-China border area in Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim; red for Jammu and Kashmir, Aksai Chin and the Pakistan border strip
advisories.regionsAffected: Border area with China, including parts of eastern Ladakh
advisories.routeImpact: The route stays outside the border strip; the width of the orange zone is not stated and cannot be mapped; Pangong, Hanle and Nubra are avoided.

advisories.level: High degree of caution for India overall; the avoid-non-essential advisory for Jammu and Kashmir excludes the Union Territory of Ladakh
advisories.routeImpact: No restriction on Leh, Sham or Hemis.

conflictRisk.note: India and Pakistan fought in May 2025 and have had a ceasefire since 10 May 2025; the LoC is far to the west and north of the route. Ladakh's border with China at Pangong, Hanle and Depsang is not visited. Leh is the base of large military formations, so photograph no military installations.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO and France stress that terrorism is persistent in India with a heightened risk in Jammu and Kashmir; Ladakh has had few incidents but is next to the Kashmir valley.

kidnappingRisk.note: No advisory cites kidnapping risk in Ladakh.

regionalRestrictions: Satellite phones, trackers and satellite-capable GPS devices without licence are illegal in India: up to 3 years in prison. Do not bring a Garmin inReach or similar; carry paper maps and the guide's local phone.
Protected Area Permits are needed for Nubra, Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri and the Hanle belt; none is needed here. The Hemis winter permit is issued in Leh.
The Srinagar-Leh road is formally advised against by France and the Manali road is closed in winter: fly to Leh.
Photography of military sites is forbidden. 2025 unrest in Leh: expect possible strikes and short curfews in Leh town, which can close the airport road.
ordinaryRisks: Acute mountain sickness, pulmonary or cerebral oedema (Leh is 3,500 m)
Flight cancellations from snow or Delhi fog
security.medicalAccess: Leh has a district hospital and army hospitals with oxygen but no advanced intensive care; Rumbak is a 3-4 hour walk from the nearest road and helicopter evacuation depends on weather and insurance authorisation. Carry a doctor-approved altitude plan and first-aid kit.
security.insuranceConsiderations: France Diplomatie requires evacuation cover that starts at the evacuation request and includes helicopter rescue; the policy must cover trekking to 4,000 m and not exclude travel against official advice. The Dutch orange zone could affect the cover if the route came near the Chinese border, so keep the route out of it.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; triggers: renewed unrest or curfew in Leh, a clarification of the Dutch orange zone, any LAC or LoC escalation, or a change in France, FCDO or US advice for Ladakh.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality; for French passport holders an e-Tourist visa (30 days, double entry) costs USD 25 from July to March plus a 2.5% bank charge and is applied for online 4-30 days before arrival. Other nationalities must check their own rule.
practicalRequirements.entry: e-Arrival card online from 72 h before travel; arrival at Delhi with the ETA printed.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months from arrival and two blank pages (standard Indian requirement; verify).
permits: Hemis National Park winter permit from the Wildlife Office in Leh (operator arranges)
No Protected Area Permit on this route
Accommodation registers guests with the C-form
practicalRequirements.insurance: High-altitude travel and helicopter evacuation insurance, starting at the evacuation request.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Mobile coverage is very limited outside Leh; foreign prepaid SIMs are often reported not to work in Ladakh (unverified), so plan for no signal in Rumbak. Satellite devices are illegal.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cash in rupees; ATMs in Leh are few and sometimes empty; homestays take cash only.
practicalRequirements.medical: Discuss acetazolamide with a doctor in France; typhoid and hepatitis A are routine; no malaria at altitude.
equipment: -20 C sleeping bag or liner for each person
Down parka, thermal layers, insulated waterproof boots
Thermos flask and spare power bank (cold drains batteries)

advantages: Two oracle festivals and a realistic snow leopard chance in the same fortnight.
Winter is the only time the hosts are free and visitors are few.
Needs no permit beyond the e-Visa and a Hemis permit, and no driving.
Mostly outside the zones that Dutch and French advice treat with caution.
Costs about EUR 2,000, far less than the guided snow leopard packages.
disadvantages: -20 C nights in unheated rooms: demanding on health, battery life and morale.
Altitude of 3,500-4,300 m, with only 48 h of acclimatisation.
Snow leopard sightings are never guaranteed.
Flights to Leh are weather-dependent and the Delhi fog adds a second layer of delay.
The Chadar and the northern circuits (Nubra, Pangong, Hanle) are excluded.
uncertainties: Festival dates rest on two operator sites following the Tibetan lunar calendar; no official 2027 calendar was readable.
Winter prices for homestays, taxis and snow leopard spotters were not obtained from the providers.
The Dutch orange zone for the China border area is not mapped; the exact extent may change.
Whether the political dispute in Ladakh flares again before February 2027.
Whether the Chadar will freeze in 2027 (it was suspended in 2026); it is not in the plan.
